problems.problem: Generic serif font (Times) and dark green color do not align with luxury perfume brand standards; professional references (e.g., Dior’s own campaign) use elegant script fonts and gold/white typography to reinforce luxury.

Background color (#DCE5D3 pale sage) and style (soft, natural leaves) differ significantly from professional references (Armani/Prive: dark with wood, Tom Ford: black with silk, Dior’s ad: gold), creating a visual gap in brand consistency.

Disconnected typography (generic Times) and background (pale sage) fail to express a cohesive luxury visual concept; the bottle (luxury) is paired with elements that lack the elegance of high-end perfume campaigns.
